data.research_question: Is group population size associated with formal state recognition?

data_preparation.policy: Only records with a positive numeric groupsize and a binary formackn value (0 or 1) are included.

normality_assessment.conclusion: At least one recognition group did not satisfy, or could not satisfy, the Shapiro-Wilk normality assessment at alpha = 0.05; therefore the two-sided non-parametric Mann-Whitney U test was selected.

statistical_test.name: Mann-Whitney U Test
statistical_test.reason: At least one recognition group did not satisfy, or could not satisfy, the Shapiro-Wilk normality assessment at alpha = 0.05; therefore the two-sided non-parametric Mann-Whitney U test was selected.

effect_size.name: Rank-biserial correlation
effect_size.direction: recognized groups tend to have larger populations

data.interpretation: There is a statistically significant difference in group population size between formally recognized and non-recognized traditional institutions. The rank-biserial correlation indicates a small effect; recognized groups tend to have larger populations.
